feature: IMPERIA CW — Cold War: archival news imagery and labelled AI colourisations

images.caption: AI-colourised interpretation of Viking 1 terrain imagery · NASA/JPL · Archival context
images.note: Added colours are an artistic interpretation, not recovered scientific colour data. The image does not depict a human Mars landing.

images.credit: NASA/JSC — S70-35368, Apollo 13 mission control, 16 April 1970
images.caption: AI-colourised NASA/JSC archive photograph · Apollo 13 mission control, 1970 · Context image
images.note: All three Apollo 13 astronauts survived. This image illustrates mission operations, not the fictional loss or nationality described by a game event.

images.caption: NASA archive photograph · Skylab, 1974 · Illustrative station imagery
images.note: Original colour photograph. It illustrates orbital stations without claiming to photograph another country's fictional spacecraft.

images.caption: US crewed Mars expedition · User-supplied alternate-history illustration
images.note: Assigned by the user to successful US crewed Mars landing and return events. This is not presented as an archival photograph.

images.caption: Soviet crewed lunar expedition · User-supplied alternate-history illustration
images.note: Assigned by the user to successful Soviet crewed lunar landing events. The historic first crewed lunar landing remains the United States in 1969.

images.caption: Soviet crewed Mars expedition · User-supplied alternate-history illustration
images.note: The user corrected the earlier Moon label: this orange landscape depicts the Soviet crewed Mars landing. The grey Soviet image remains assigned to the Moon.

images.caption: French crewed lunar expedition · User-supplied alternate-history illustration
images.note: Assigned by the user to successful French crewed lunar landing events. It is an illustration of an alternative game outcome, not an archival photograph.

images.caption: Saudi crewed lunar expedition
images.note: Assigned by the user to accepted Saudi crewed lunar landing and Earth recovery. Native news uses a cover crop anchored to retain the flag and helmet; no credit or caption is shown in the game.
